introduction.definition: A gear assembly transmits rotation and torque between shafts through meshing teeth. In this spur train a driving pinion turns an idler, which turns a larger driven gear; the output turns three times slower with about three times the torque, and the idler reverses direction without changing the ratio.

pressure.title: Pitch circles roll; force acts along the line of action
pressure.description: Mating gears behave like pitch circles rolling without slipping: speed ratio = z_driven / z_driver (here 48/16 = 3; the idler changes direction only). Tooth force acts along the line of action at the pressure angle (20°), splitting into a tangential (torque) and a separating (radial) component that the bearings carry. Correct centre distance gives the designed backlash; contact pattern, lubrication and alignment decide gear life (pitting, scuffing, tooth breakage).

video_tutorials.title: Gear Assembly — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Gear Assembly.
A gear assembly transmits rotation and torque between shafts through meshing teeth.

In this spur train a driving pinion turns an idler, which turns a larger driven gear; the output turns three times slower with about three times the torque, and the idler reverses direction without changing the ratio.
Typical applications include gearboxes, machine tools and conveyors; pump and compressor speed increasers / reducers.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Driving Pinion (z = 16) on Keyed Shaft, Idler Gear (z = 24) — reverses direction, ratio unchanged on Keyed Shaft, Driven Gear (z = 48) on Keyed Shaft.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Gear Assembly works.
The pinion drives the idler.
The idler reverses direction.
The driven gear turns slower with more torque.
Bearings carry tooth forces.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Mating gears behave like pitch circles rolling without slipping: speed ratio = z_driven / z_driver (here 48/16 = 3; the idler changes direction only).

video_tutorials.title: Gear Assembly — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Gear Assembly.
Listen for noise; check temperature.
Check backlash and contact pattern; oil analysis.
Replace worn gears / bearings.
Watch for pitting: noise, vibration at mesh frequency. Common cause: overload, poor lubrication.
Watch for tooth breakage: sudden stop. Common cause: shock load, fatigue.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
